high_level_description: A wordless documentary gouache illustration of a French ceramics dealer in 1970 unpacking three independently issued narrative plate series from Creil, Creil-Montereau, and Digoin, each production choosing a different La Fontaine fable and retaining its own clay body, border, and printing palette within an ordinary shop without prize display.

compositional_deconstruction.background: A modest French ceramics shop in 1970 has whitewashed plaster walls, a pale limestone floor, exposed dark ceiling beams, and one tall leaded window admitting neutral daylight from the left. The irregular room contains no stage, museum vitrine, central pedestal, symmetrical display, prize, crown, badge, arrow, diagram, inscription, letter, numeral, label, or advertising poster.

elements.desc: Long oak dealer table angled from lower left toward upper right, crowded naturally with plain linen wrapping cloths, loose straw, three folded towels, and two undecorated packing boards. Its worn rectangular top supports the ceramic consignments at different depths, functioning as an ordinary unpacking surface rather than a formal exhibition and judging table.

Ceramics dealer standing behind the table, adult woman with medium-brown skin and dark brown hair gathered in a low bun, wearing a cream blouse, rust cardigan, dark navy skirt, and white work apron. She carefully lifts one creamware plate edgewise from the left consignment while comparing its black rim treatment with the neighboring series; her hands hold no judging instrument.

Shallow straw-lined wooden crate containing an early Creil narrative series in cream-colored round earthenware. One front-facing plate carries a crisp black transfer-printed scene of two rats beside an egg and fox. Four plates remain stacked beneath it, showing only matching rims decorated with alternating black griffins and lyres; no writing appears.

Rectangular wooden delivery box containing a later Creil-Montereau series of white ironstone. One front-facing plate uses sepia transfer printing with restrained blue and ochre touches to show a rooster and fox across three pictorial moments inside a thin gold rim. Four plates remain stacked beneath, revealing only repeated sepia edges without captions or numbers.

Low woven hamper containing a Digoin narrative series in white feldspathic faience. One front-facing dessert plate has a basket-weave relief rim and blue-gray printed vignette of a cat meeting a fox. Four smaller plates remain separated by folded cloth beneath it, their matching relief rims identifying this delivery without exposed writing or invented maker marks.
